title: Modified acid-PAGE method for rapid screening and phenotyping of wheat gliadin mutant lines
author: Watry, Zerkle, et al.

steps.title: Extract gliadin proteins
steps.instruction: Separate glutenin and gliadin fractions by adding 70 % ethanol to milled wheat flour; use about 10 mg milled flour per genotype for phenotyping, and use flour from the crushed brush‑end of half‑seeds for mutant screening (the embryo‑end half‑seeds are retained for planting).

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Place the gel cassette in the electrophoresis apparatus and run the A‑PAGE until the dye front reaches the bottom, typically 90–100 min (approximately half the time of the original lactate‑lactic acid method).

steps.title: Stain gel with Coomassie
steps.instruction: Shake the Coomassie stain solution well, add 50 mL to a gel‑staining box, remove the gel from its cassette with a metal spatula, place the gel in the box, cover with a lid, and shake at about 50 rpm at room temperature; stain overnight for convenience (minimum 4 h).

substeps.instruction: Add 50 mL stain to staining box.
Pry cassette apart with metal spatula and transfer gel.
Cover box and shake at ~50 rpm, room temperature.

steps.title: Dispose of used stain
steps.instruction: When protein bands are visible, discard the Coomassie stain solution according to local hazardous‑waste guidelines (the solution is ~pH 1.8 and contains methanol).

steps.title: De‑stain gel
steps.instruction: Rinse the gel 2–3 times with water, then de‑stain in fresh water on an orbital shaker for 15 min with shaking; repeat rinsing and de‑staining cycles until the desired background level is achieved.

substeps.instruction: Place gel in water on orbital shaker, shake for 15 min.
Repeat rinse and de‑stain cycles until satisfactory.
